title: Gulf Crescent Motif Mehndi Design for Finger
descriptionParagraphs: This gulf design sits on the fingers. The main fill is floral vine, with bell garland worked around it. It's a medium-level design, and it suits Diwali.

Finger designs are quick to apply and dry fast, which makes them practical when time is short. Fingertips have thicker skin, so the stain there usually develops darker than on the rest of the hand. This pattern suits someone who is already comfortable with basic lines, dots and petals and wants to practise even spacing.
Designs usually flow diagonally across the hand instead of covering it completely. A henna night before the wedding is a long-standing custom in Gulf weddings.
Application tips: Use a slightly wider cone tip to get the thick outlines that define the Gulf look. Leave clear gaps between motifs; the empty space is part of the style.

image.alt: Gulf Crescent Motif mehndi design for finger henna pattern

faq.q: What is Khaleeji henna?
faq.a: It is the henna style of the Arabian Gulf countries: bold floral motifs with thick outlines and open space.

faq.q: How is Gulf henna different from Indian mehndi?
faq.a: Gulf designs are larger and more open, while Indian mehndi is finer and covers more of the skin.

faq.q: Is Gulf-style henna quick to apply?
faq.a: Usually, yes. The larger motifs and open spacing mean a hand can be finished much faster than a dense design.

title: Gulf Mesh Jaal Mehndi Design for Finger
descriptionParagraphs: Look at the butterfly wing first, then the paisley that frames it. This one is made for the fingers and is one for experienced hands. Wear it for Teej.

Finger designs are quick to apply and dry fast, which makes them practical when time is short. Fingertips have thicker skin, so the stain there usually develops darker than on the rest of the hand. This is a detailed pattern usually done by an experienced artist; allow plenty of time and work in small sections.

title: Gulf Mesh Jaal Mehndi Design for Full Hand
